h1: Intelligence Layer — AI & SaaS Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product, captured at 1462x1080 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product — a logo row, 0.9s transitions, a moving marquee and #050505 base.
about: Intelligence Layer shows one way to build the landing page for an AI or SaaS product, and publishes the instructions that produced it. The colour scheme is near-black #050505 underneath and #FAFAFA for the type, and the page is set in Manrope. Delivery is one self-contained HTML file, captured at 1462x1080 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Motion is confined to 0.9s transitions, cubic-bezier(.22, 1.36, 1) and a looping video bed. Keep it open while you write: the 11,825-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: Top row, one action
layout.body: Navigation is a single row with no second level under it. The bar sits over the 1462x1080 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Values you can check
layout.body: The brief names the numbers: 100vh sections, 25px spacing steps, 0.9s transitions and cubic-bezier(.22, 1.36, 1) easing. That is why the composition holds together, because there is no invented spacing step between the type and the frame. The list is short enough that a reviewer can check it element by element.

layout.title: The scale is the styling
layout.body: Typography is Manrope, and the brief assigns the face a job rather than mixing for variety. Weight, tracking and size steps are all specified, so the hierarchy survives a substitution. Tracking is set per size, so the display line and the caption do not share one letter-spacing value. One face, clear roles.

layout.title: The nav is deliberately thin
layout.body: The bar is a handful of elements, so it rebuilds without a component library. The reference was captured at 1462x1080.

motion.title: The canvas is the visual
motion.body: The first screen is built by the browser rather than shipped as an image: a WebGL canvas. The render carries its own colour, so the palette around it is kept quiet. Keep the interface flat around it.

motion.title: Timings in milliseconds
motion.body: The controls resolve in 0.9s, fast enough that the page answers as it is touched rather than after it. Easing is specified alongside the duration (0.9s), so a rebuild cannot quietly substitute a different feel.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over near-black #050505, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.

editorial.title: How the landing page reflows
editorial.body: A designed narrow layout takes more decisions than a squeeze. The brief pays for them: the scale is fluid rather than stepped, the section is held at 100vh and the motion has a reduced-motion branch, stated rather than discovered at build time. The hierarchy is what survives the reflow.

editorial.title: Reading Intelligence Layer as a spec
editorial.body: Type is the first number: 100vh sections and 25px spacing steps. The spacing follows from it, and everything else on the page is positioned against those two values. Nothing in this landing page depends on a default.

editorial.title: Making the landing page yours
editorial.body: Re-skinning the palette first is the usual mistake. It changes the mood without touching the composition, and 100vh sections and 25px spacing steps still carry the layout; do the copy and media first and the palette last. Rewrite the copy and the media before you re-colour anything.

faq.question: Do I need one self-contained HTML file to rebuild Intelligence Layer?
faq.answer: Intelligence Layer was built in one self-contained HTML file, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: What does the brief behind Intelligence Layer actually contain?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 1462x1080, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: Can I keep the Intelligence Layer transitions and change the timings?
faq.answer: Entrances and state changes are in the 0.9s range using cubic-bezier(.22, 1.36, 1) with a reduced-motion branch in the brief. They are driven by state changes rather than a scroll library, and they never hold up the copy.

audience: The landing page is aimed at teams that already know one self-contained HTML file and only need cubic-bezier(.22, 1.36, 1) easing written down.
